correctness.rationale: The proof is exhaustive and boundary-safe. Any dominating set meeting both bipartition sides has a unique largest selected \(A\)-class index \(i\) and smallest selected \(B\)-class index \(j\). Domination forces all \(A_t\) with \(t<j\) and all \(B_t\) with \(t>i\), and feasibility is exactly \(j\le i+1\). The case \(j=i+1\) gives the unique cut set \(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_i\cup B_{i+1}\cup\cdots\cup B_p\); the case \(j\le i\) gives nonempty choices in \(A_i,B_j\), arbitrary choices in intervening classes, and the displayed monomial shift. One-sided dominating sets are precisely the two endpoint cuts. The resulting cases are disjoint and exhaustive. Independently, 77 canonical instances with \(p\le3\) and all class sizes in \(\{1,2\}\) were brute-force enumerated over every vertex subset and matched the closed polynomial exactly.

value.rationale: Ordinary domination is a standard graph invariant and chain graphs are a canonical hereditary bipartite class. The result completely enumerates all dominating sets for arbitrary twin-class multiplicities, not merely the minimum size, and yields the total count and domination number as immediate consequences. The extremal-class decomposition is a reusable structural description rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
residual_risks: The formula is class-specific and does not address algorithmic complexity beyond this graph family.

final_claim: For every connected finite chain graph with canonical nonempty twin classes \(A_1,\ldots,A_p\) and \(B_1,\ldots,B_p\), where \(N(a)=B_1\cup\cdots\cup B_i\) for \(a\in A_i\), the ordinary domination polynomial is exactly the boundary-pair formula in RESULT.md: the \(p+1\) cut sets plus, for each \(1\le j\le i\le p\), all sets with extremal selected classes \(A_i\) and \(B_j\), forced outside classes, and arbitrary intervening classes. The stated specialization at \(x=1\) counts all dominating sets, and \(\gamma(G)=1\) exactly when one side has size one, otherwise \(\gamma(G)=2\).
limitations: Connected chain graphs with nonempty canonical twin classes only; disconnected chain graphs are not separately classified.
The claim is the ordinary domination polynomial, not independent, total, paired, restrained, Roman, or other domination variants.
